   STAFF REPORT
Meeting Date:  January 30, 2024
To:  Arts and Culture Council Liaisons Mayor Dr. Julian Gold, MD &
  Councilmember Lili Bosse
From:  Matthew Brown, Recreation Services Manager
  Corrina Lesser, Recreation Supervisor
Subject:  Recommendation by the Arts and Culture Commission for the second
  annual Festival Beverly Hills

Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION

The inaugural Festival Beverly Hills event was held on Sunday, March 12, 2023, at the
Beverly Hills Farmers Market, and included performances and hands-on family friendly
activities from more than 15 artists and organizations including:

  •  Cultural performances and tutorials from organizations like the Asian Arts Dance
  Team, Blue13, Cortines High School, Self Help Graphics & Art, and Southern
  California Marimba
  •  Culinary programs with a teen cooking competition and an Iranian spice-making
  workshop
  •  Iconic Southern California-based organizations like Bob Baker Marionette
  Theatre, dublab Community Radio, LA Carnivale, and LA Commons
  •  Performances by Beverly Hills Unified School District music production and
  dance students

Festival Beverly Hills aims to celebrate and showcase the cultural diversity of the City of
Beverly Hills and Southern California. Through a range of performances, family-friendly
workshops, activities, and culinary offerings, Festival Beverly Hills exemplifies the City
as a world-class arts and cultural destination. The objective of the Arts and Culture
Commission and Community Services Department staff for the second annual Festival
Beverly Hills, is to build upon the success of the inaugural festival and continue to
elevate Festival Beverly Hills as a cultural destination for both the Beverly Hills
community and the Greater Southern California region.
 Meeting Date: January 30, 2024

DISCUSSION
Although the Beverly Hills Farmers Market was a successful venue for the inaugural
festival, in an effort to give the event space a larger and more distinctive footprint, the
Arts and Culture Commission recommend relocating the festival to Roxbury Park in 2024
and beyond. Roxbury Park, which also plays host to other popular Community Services
Department events like Beverly Hills Doggy Daze 90210 and the Beverly Hills Day of
Wellness, provides a more flexible and dynamic venue, allowing for continued expansion
and elevation as a world-class cultural event. Additional parking can be provided for
attendees at nearby Beverly Hills High School.

The inaugural Festival Beverly Hills event was scheduled for early spring in 2023 and
experienced several scheduling obstacles. Obstacles and considerations to continue
Festival Beverly Hills as a recurring spring event, include increased chances of
inclement spring weather, the number of seasonal holiday dates, and several ongoing
Community Services Department and City-wide programs activities, and events.
Specifically, some of the logistical challenges in the spring include the ongoing need to
plan for a date not in conflict with the Los Angeles marathon, the Vanity Fair party, and
the Easter holidays. Planning for a mid-summer event aligns in the calendar roughly
midway between the fall and spring art shows, which is optimal from an event production
and overall event calendar perspective. The Arts and Culture Commission propose that
Festival Beverly Hills be moved to a summer event, and scheduled to occur either
Sunday, July 21 or Sunday, July 28 in 2024.

These dates and placement on the summer calendar will help avoid the spring season
scheduling challenges and provide an opportunity to engage a wider audience
demographic of residents and visitors to the region alike. The summer season festival
date also provides an increased opportunity to secure featured talent and deploy a more
robust festival marketing and promotional strategy.

Staff are seeking approval, on recommendation from the Arts & Culture Commission, to
schedule the second annual Festival Beverly Hills on either Sunday July 21, 2024, or
Sunday, July 28, 2024, and approve the recommendation to relocate the event from the
Beverly Hills Farmer’s Market to Roxbury Park.

FISCAL IMPACT
The costs for the 2024 Festival Beverly Hills will be absorbed within the current
Community Services Department budget.

RECOMMENDATION
The Arts and Culture Commission and staff recommend the Arts and Culture Council
Liaisons support the proposed scheduling of Festival Beverly Hills as a summer event at
Roxbury Park, to occur in July 2024.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By

CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive

  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Arts and Culture Commission Committee
  Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, January 30, 2024
  4:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 30, 2024 / 4:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian Gold, Councilmember Lili Bosse, City Manager Nancy Coffey,
  recreational Services Manager Matthew Brown, Director of Community
  Services Stephanie Harris, Arts and Culture Commission Vice Chair Karla
  Gordy Bristol, Arts and Culture Commissioner Liliana Filipovic

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Recommendation by the Arts and Culture Commission for the second annual
  Festival Beverly Hills:
  a. Presentation by Matthew Brown.
  i. Recap of Festival Beverly Hills 2023.
  1. Occurred on Sunday March 12, 2023, from 8 AM to 1 PM at the
  Beverly Hills Farmers Market.
  2. The event was well attended and received positive feedback from
  both attendees and participants.
  3. Events included cultural performances and tutorials from
  organizations including the Asian Arts Dance Team, Blue 13 Dance,
  Bollywood Pop Up Dance Tutorial, Cortines High School, self-help
  graphics and art, a stencil and screen-printing workshop, Southern
  California Marimba, as well as numerous culinary elements.
  ii. The festival in 2024 is proposed as relocating to Roxbury Park to increase
  the space available to the festival due to the 2023 festival hitting the space
  constraints of the Farmers Market.
  iii. Roxbury Park already hosts similar sized events such as Doggy Daze
  90210 and the Day of Wellness events.
  iv. Beverly Hills High School can be used for additional parking, with people
  being transported between the two sites by shuttle like what happens
  during the aforementioned events.
  v. The event is also proposed as moving to the summer instead of the spring,
  which would place it midway between the spring and fall art shows.
  vi. Staff is currently planning for this year’s festival to be on either Sunday July
  21st or Sunday July 28th.
 Highlights for January 30, 2024
Arts and Culture Commission Committee

  vii. A summer event offers increased opportunities for attendance by both
  residents and tourists as well as increased options for entertainment.
  b.  Roxbury offers both sports areas, which could be rapidly converted into a concert
  venue as well as indoor areas to store instruments in a secure area.
  c.  A multitude of options for hours of operation of the event have been discussed,
  with staff favoring an afternoon alignment that can potentially run into the evening.
  d.  Councilmember Bosse recommends that the Arts and Culture commission reach
  out to the CVB and Chamber of Commerce to bring in additional tourists and local
  businesses.
  e.  If the commission wants to make this an annual event, they should consider
  acquiring banners to advertise the event.
  f.  Youth sports leagues do not use the park in July and August, which is one of the
  reasons why that time was selected.
  g.  The event’s operating hours are currently budgeted for, but should the council
  direct the event to have longer operating hours, the budget of the event would have
  to be increased.
  h.  The current budget for the event is $20,000.
  i.  The commission is planning between $3,500 and $5,000 on one or two anchor
  performers, with the rest of the performances coming in between $500 and $1,500.

  3) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: January 30, 2024 / 4:36 PM
